For use in my RV - I have a "short bus" style of RV - y'know, the kind like a truck with a camper on the back, but a little bigger. Not much, just about the size of the buses for those with disabilities. It works for me, but the sink really isn't large enough to hold all my dishes after cooking and yes, I do cook most of my meals when I'm out exploring in the RV. I have actually tried this dishwasher in my house completely hooked up to the faucet with hot water and found that it works great that way should you have problems with your big dishwasher and are waiting for the person to come fix it, this little dishwasher can keep your dishes clean without you having to stand over the sink. Now, as far as working with this in the RV, I boiled a pot of water outside, added some cool water and then poured this still-hot water into the dishwasher's reservoir and then plugged it in to wash dishes. It's one more step - to heat the water - but it really wasn't that big a deal since I was set up at my camp spot and had a rocket stove sitting outside the RV. The rocket stove heats up fast on just a few twigs and holds a good-sized pot easily. The water boils fast enough and if I'd had a shorter extension cord, I could have had the Gizmo dishwasher next to the rocket stove, its drainage hose in a bucket beneath it. That may be my normal set up - easier to eat, scrape off the dirty dishes, put them right in the Gizmo and wash right then and there. But the main thing is, I really like this little dishwasher and I did have my reservations considering the size of my RV and the size of this dishwasher, but after weighing my options (hand wash in a plastic tub because the RV's sink is too small) I figured taking a chance on this machine was worth it. It was definitely worth it! Small enough to store when not in use, very portable and able to be used in different ways, this is perfect for on the road!
